story_clusters.headline: US and Lithuania conduct joint HIMARS live-fire exercises
story_clusters.summary: American and Lithuanian forces completed integrated High Mobility Artillery Rocket System training with live-fire exercises at Kairiai training area. The exercises marked the culmination of the HIMARS apprenticeship program, aimed at advancing Lithuanian artillery capabilities on NATO's eastern flank.

story_clusters.headline: Coalition tensions rise over Žemaitaitis criminal connections
story_clusters.summary: Prime Minister Ruginienė faces criticism for her handling of revelations about Dawn of Nemunas leader Remigijus Žemaitaitis's ties to criminal figure Aurelijus Perminas. Former prime ministers called her response irresponsible, while Žemaitaitis disclosed renting his car to the party for €31,500.

story_clusters.headline: Baltic states establish unified military mobility zone
story_clusters.summary: Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia agreed to eliminate bureaucratic barriers for military movement between their territories, creating a unified mobility space to strengthen NATO's eastern flank defense. The initiative allows rapid cross-border deployment of forces and equipment among the three Baltic allies.

story_clusters.headline: President Nausėda's property under construction inspection
story_clusters.summary: State Construction Inspection received complaints and launched an investigation into President Gitanas Nausėda's Vilnius property to determine if construction violated state land boundaries. The inspection follows public concerns about potential regulatory violations.

story_clusters.headline: Environment deputy minister dismissed amid security concerns
story_clusters.summary: Environment Minister Kastytis Žuromskis dismissed deputy minister Edmundas Mačieža, prompting Prime Minister Ruginienė to seek explanations about the circumstances surrounding the unexpected termination. The dismissal occurred during a National Security Committee meeting.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The partisan resistance narrative serves as the legitimating mythology of the post-1990 state; any political movement that challenges it (whether from the left via Soviet nostalgia or from outside via Holocaust accountability) faces structural opposition from the state historical apparatus.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The "double genocide" framework is institutionally embedded in museums, historical commissions, and criminal law (Article 99 of the Criminal Code expands the definition of genocide to include political/social groups), and will resist revision absent sustained external pressure.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The founding mythology is transmitted through at least six national holidays and a network of state-funded museums and commissions; it is not dependent on any single party and will persist across government changes.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Lithuania's geographic vulnerability is permanent and unreducible by diplomacy; it can only be mitigated by forward-deployed allied forces and physical fortification.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The Suwałki Gap will remain NATO's most critical single-point-of-failure so long as Kaliningrad hosts significant Russian military capability and Belarus remains aligned with Moscow.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Klaipėda port constitutes a strategic single point of failure: its destruction or blockade would simultaneously eliminate Lithuania's maritime trade, LNG-based energy independence, and NATO seaborne resupply.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Lithuania's defense spending trajectory (5–6% of GDP by 2026–2030) is a direct function of geographic proximity to Russia; any reduction would signal a revision of threat assessment, not a policy preference.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The Soviet institutional inheritance — energy dependency, broad-gauge rail, Russian-speaking industrial towns (Visaginas), and a shadow economy estimated at 24.7% of GDP — continues to generate measurable policy costs more than three decades after independence.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: EU/NATO accession (2004) functioned as the primary post-imperial institutional reconstruction mechanism; without it, Lithuania's institutional trajectory would more closely resemble Belarus or Moldova.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Lithuania's lustration was formally strict but practically incomplete; former nomenklatura networks persisted through the transition and only generational replacement, not institutional action, is fully dissolving them.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The urban-rural cleavage, not ethnicity, is the primary axis of Lithuanian political competition; ethnic minority parties will continue to lose vote share as generational replacement advances.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Lithuania's "zero option" citizenship policy was the single most consequential cleavage-management decision of the independence period; it structurally prevented the ethno-political mobilization that destabilized Latvia and Estonia.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The Polish minority's political influence will continue declining absent a reversal of its demographic trajectory (lowest share among youngest cohorts: 5.3% among ages 0–9 vs. 7.2% among ages 50–59).
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Lithuania's population will not stabilize above 2.5 million without sustained positive net migration; natural population dynamics alone guarantee continued decline through at least 2060.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The defense spending commitment (5–6% of GDP) and the demographic contraction create a structural fiscal vise: a shrinking tax base must fund expanding military obligations.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Immigration from non-EU countries (Ukraine, Belarus, Central Asia) is transforming Lithuania's demographic profile faster than any domestic political actor anticipated; foreigners increased from 2.5% to 7.5% of population in four years, creating integration pressures that will generate political mobilization.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Lithuania's economic convergence with the EU average (46% → 87% of EU average GDP in PPP in 20 years) is the most powerful structural argument for the EU accession model in the post-Soviet space.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Scandinavian bank dominance (56% of assets) creates a transmission channel through which Nordic financial sector stress would propagate directly into the Lithuanian economy.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The defense spending target (5–6% of GDP) is fiscally achievable only through a combination of debt accumulation, tax increases, and EU fund reallocation; the IMF's 60%-by-2030 debt warning establishes the binding constraint.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The post-2022 trade reorientation away from Russia is essentially complete and irreversible; the remaining 2% of exports to Russia represents residual transit, not dependency.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The Baltic grid synchronization (February 2025) was the single most consequential infrastructure event in Lithuania's post-independence history: it eliminated the last major Soviet-era systemic dependency and physically embedded Lithuania in the European energy architecture.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Rail Baltica's completion (target 2030) will determine whether Lithuania's infrastructure reorientation is fully achieved; its failure or significant delay would leave the 1,520mm broad-gauge Soviet rail network as the dominant freight corridor, maintaining residual eastward orientation.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Lithuania's energy infrastructure now has built-in redundancy (LNG terminal + GIPL pipeline + LitPol Link + NordBalt + grid synchronization); no single point of energy infrastructure failure can restore Russian energy leverage.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: The Ignalina decommissioning cost (~€3.4 billion through 2049, 95% externally funded) represents the largest single financial liability inherited from the Soviet period and will remain a fiscal and technical burden for another 23 years.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.

structural_claim_status.claim_text: Lithuania's infrastructure pivot — from nearly 100% Soviet energy dependency to effective energy independence in 11 years (2014–2025) — constitutes the fastest and most complete energy security reorientation achieved by any former Soviet state.
structural_claim_status.evidence_summary: Baseline — not yet tested against weekly evidence.
